Round-7 FAIL re-checked from scratch: the algorithm is now right. _invert computes Decimal(1)/Decimal(value) (28-digit context), takes the leading-digit exponent from the quotient itself, quantizes to 8 significant digits with ROUND_HALF_EVEN, and re-quantizes one digit coarser when rounding carried into a new leading digit. I wrote an independent exact reference (Fraction arithmetic, integer half-even rounding, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify8-data-tooling/scripts/invert_probe.py) and compared it with _invert on 200,453 inputs (200,000 random decimals with 0-6 places, every 10^p +/- k*10^(p-9) for p=-3..3, k=-30..30, and the test cases) and on all 125,897 distinct OBS_VALUEs of the downloaded H10_data.xml: 0 mismatches. Round-7 probes now give _invert('1.0000000051')='0.99999999', _invert('10.000000051')='0.099999999', _invert('100.00000051')='0.0099999999'; carry case _invert('0.1000000004')='10.000000' (8 digits). The committed snapshots are unaffected: the live refetch with the new code and my independent rebuild are both byte-identical to the committed CSVs (rows data-*-snapshot). One caveat on the docstring: the quotient is rounded to 28 digits before the 8-digit rounding, so 'exact quotient' is exact for every input of fewer than about 20 digits; it cannot matter for H.10/H.15 quotes (4-5 decimals).

rows.location: tests/test_fetch_data.py test_inversion_keeps_eight_significant_digits_in_plain_decimal (comment '# Ties go to even, on the exact quotient.')
rows.evidence: Checked at HEAD 8da4051 (identical to 7cdab4c outside ledgers/: `git diff 7cdab4c HEAD --name-only` lists only ledger files). New row (new hunk). The two cases under the comment '# Ties go to even, on the exact quotient.' are ('0.8','1.2500000') and ('1.6','0.62500000'). Their exact quotients are 1.25 and 0.625, which terminate within eight significant digits, so neither is a tie. Mutation test (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify8-data-tooling/scripts/mut_all.py; fresh pyc each run): replacing every ROUND_HALF_EVEN with ROUND_HALF_UP in tools/fetch_data.py leaves all 43 tests in tests/test_fetch_data.py passing (mutant SURVIVED). _invert's docstring promises 'rounded (half to even)' and the test comment claims it is pinned, but nothing pins it. A true tie exists: 1/4096 = 0.000244140625 exactly (nine significant digits ending in 5); half-even gives 0.00024414062 (current code) and half-up gives 0.00024414063. (Only 1/(4096*10^k) can be a tie: a terminating quotient has significand 5^m, and 5^12 = 244140625 is the only power of 5 with nine digits.) The behaviour is correct; the test and its comment are not.
rows.fix: In tests/test_fetch_data.py, replace the comment and the two cases under '# Ties go to even, on the exact quotient.' by ('4096', '0.00024414062') and ('0.4096', '2.4414062') (1/4096 = 0.000244140625 and 1/0.4096 = 2.44140625 are exact ties at the ninth digit; half-even rounds down to the even 2), keeping '0.8' and '1.6' only as ordinary cases under a comment that does not mention ties. Then confirm a ROUND_HALF_UP mutant of tools/fetch_data.py fails the test.
